incidente.resumo: Steam suffered a widespread outage of about 2 hours on May 7th, with users unable to log in or use the Steam store and the Steam API unavailable from many locations. A third-party monitoring analysis saw paths from several upstream ISPs not reaching Steam's data center and routes to Valve's network no longer advertised, and its best guess is a routing configuration change by Steam. The text does not say how service was restored.

descricao.texto: Users around the world reported being unable to log in or use the Steam store; the third-party monitoring of the Steam API saw a dramatic drop in API availability. The text does not say how Valve first noticed the problem.
trechos: There were reports of users around the world of being unable to login or use the Steam store.
The first thing we noticed was a dramatic drop in API availability, as shown in Figure 2.

descricao.texto: The authors' best guess, based on the evidence, is that a routing configuration change by Steam caused the outage. They observed massive BGP routing instability, routes to Steam (Valve network AS32590) other than via Qwest no longer advertised, and paths from Level 3, Telia and Abovenet/Zayo not reaching the Steam data center.
trechos: Based on the evidence, our best guess is that a routing configuration change by Steam was the cause of the outage.
At the BGP layer we can see massive routing instability (Figure 8).
Looking at the AS paths themselves, we see over time that Qwest is being preferred while other routes to Steam (Valve network AS32590) are no longer advertised (Figure 9).
During the outage, traffic paths from Comcast and Qwest are successfully reaching the Steam data center, but paths from other upstream ISPs—Level 3, Telia and Abovenet/Zayo—are not (Figure 7).

descricao.texto: The authors' best guess is a routing configuration change by Steam; the exact change is not identified.
trechos: Based on the evidence, our best guess is that a routing configuration change by Steam was the cause of the outage.
Starting at 11:45 Pacific on May 7th and lasting for 2 hours, the popular online gaming service Steam suffered a widespread outage.

observacoes: Third-party analysis by a monitoring vendor based on its own measurements; there is no statement from Valve. The year of the incident is not in the extracted text. status_relatorio is preliminar because the authors say they will update the post if Steam releases a post-mortem. The closing section on monitoring data center ingress is general advice ending in a product call to action, not prevention by the affected company.
